name: Edge/CDN per-customer rate-limit & abuse
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: The edge/CDN per-customer rate-limit segment is the densest 'counter-store at the edge' competitive landscape in beava's use-case map, and 2025-2026 reshaped it more than any year prior. Six archetypes matter: (A) Cloudflare Durable Objects - SQLite-backed since 2024, with the per-Object storage cap raised to 10 GB on Workers Paid plan, soft ~1 k req/s per Object, strongly consistent within an Object, billed for SQLite storage from January 7, 2026 onward (Workers Free plan exempt); Durable Object Facets announced at Agents Week 2026 lets Dynamic Workers instantiate per-tenant isolated SQLite DOs - the structural answer for any Cloudflare-fronted buyer. (B) Cloudflare Workers Rate Limiting API GA September 19, 2025 (ratelimit binding) - free-with-Workers, sub-ms inline, built directly on DO/edge state - the hyperscaler-bundled default. (C) Fastly Edge Rate Limiting GA - ratecounter (VCL + Compute) with the 200 000-entries-per-site LRU cap and penaltybox primitive; Fastly KV Store GA (1 000 writes/s, 5 000 reads/s per store). (D) Cloudflare native Rate Limiting Rules (WAF zone level) + AWS WAF rate-based rules + Akamai Aggregated Rate Limiting (announced Nov 2025) + Azure Front Door / API Management throttling - the 'WAF tab on your CDN dashboard' set. (E) Upstash Redis - the de facto serverless rate-limit backend via @upstash/ratelimit on Vercel / Cloudflare / Deno / Netlify / Supabase, HTTP-REST-over-fetch (Mar 2025 free tier: 500 k commands/mo, $0.20 per 100 k commands, $0.25/GB storage, 200 GB egress free) - Source Available license under the Upstash terms; pulls in the (post-Apr-2024 RSALv2/SSPLv1 or post-May-2025 AGPLv3) Redis license posture. (F) Self-hosted distributed rate-limit services: Gubernator (Mailgun, Apache-2.0, ~2 000 batched RPS/node sub-ms, no external cache, token-bucket + leaky-bucket), Envoy Rate Limit (Apache-2.0, Lyft, Redis-backed), Apache APISIX limit-count/limit-req/limit-conn + AI Rate Limiting (Apache-2.0, 100+ plugins zero paywall, token-level LLM rate limiting), NVIDIA go-ratelimit (Apache-2.0), Tyk DRL (in-cluster distributed counter), Kong Rate Limiting Advanced (Enterprise license required for the advanced/Redis-cluster strategy). Zuplo programmable rate limiter (TypeScript, globally-synchronised across 300+ edge POPs) is the closest 'managed edge-native counter' competitor. Adjacent KV / counter substrates: Deno KV (strongly-consistent, 35 regions, on FoundationDB; 1 GiB / 15 k reads-day / 10 k writes-day free), Vercel KV (Upstash-backed) + Edge Config (read-mostly), Supabase Edge Functions (Deno runtime, Upstash-redis or Postgres-via-PgBouncer pattern), Bunny/Gcore sovereign-edge stacks (less explicit on the counter primitive), Aerospike + ScyllaDB + Memcached/Twemproxy at the very top end (Cloudflare's own per-PoP Rust+Twemproxy+Memcached system documented in 'Counting Things - a lot of different things'). On the billing-meter side specifically: OpenMeter (Apache-2.0, Kafka + ClickHouse, processes 'millions of usage events per minute'), Lago (Apache-2.0, 1 M events/s on ClickHouse), Metronome (acquired by Stripe Jan 2026 to become Stripe Billing Meter Events / Meter Event Streams v2), Orb, Schematic, Stripe Meters native.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Per-edge-platform incumbent: Cloudflare = Workers Rate Limiting API (GA Sept 19 2025) + Durable Objects SQLite (10 GB/object, billing from Jan 7 2026) + WAF Rate Limiting Rules + Bot Management (Enterprise add-on, hundreds of billions of req/day training data, per-customer behavioral baselines launched Nov 2025) + Web Bot Auth / HTTP Message Signatures (Agents Week 2026; co-adopted by Amazon/Akamai/OpenAI/AWS WAF/Vercel/Shopify); Fastly = Edge Rate Limiting GA (ratecounter VCL + Compute, 200 k entries/site LRU) + KV Store GA; Netlify = Netlify Rate Limiting GA + Netlify Blobs; Vercel = Edge Middleware + Vercel KV (Upstash-backed) + Edge Config (read-mostly); Deno Deploy = Deno KV (strongly-consistent, 35 regions, 1 GiB/15 k reads/10 k writes-day free); Supabase = Edge Functions (Deno, 2 s CPU cap, gateway-level rate limit + Upstash-redis pattern, EF047 error code); Akamai = EdgeWorkers + EdgeKV + Aggregated Rate Limiting (announced Nov 2025) + Bot Manager + Noname Security ($450 M acquisition Jun 2024); AWS = API Gateway Usage Plans (default 10 k RPS, 5 k burst) + WAF rate-based rules + Bot Control + Bedrock Gateway. Per-API-gateway vendor: Kong Rate Limiting Advanced (Redis or local-cluster, Enterprise license required for advanced strategies), Apigee Quota policy (Google, JS/Java callouts), Tyk DRL, Apache APISIX limit-count/limit-req/limit-conn + AI Rate Limiting (Apache-2.0, zero paywall), KrakenD, Zuplo (programmable, globally-synchronised across 300+ POPs by default), Mulesoft, AWS API Gateway. Per-AI-gateway vendor: Cloudflare AI Gateway (fixed or sliding rate limits but lacks token-level budgets), Portkey (1 600+ models, enterprise governance), Helicone (token-based rate limiting via Helicone-User-Id, multi-policy stacking by both request count AND cost), LiteLLM, TrueFoundry, Envoy AI Gateway, Kong AI Rate Limiting Advanced (Enterprise), Apache APISIX AI Rate Limiting (token-level, OSS), Azure API Management llm-token-limit policy. Per-usage-metering: Stripe Billing Meter Events / Meter Event Streams v2 (post-Metronome acquisition Jan 2026), OpenMeter (Apache-2.0, YC-backed), Lago (Apache-2.0, 1 M EPS), Orb (250 k+ EPS), Schematic, Trigger.dev (named public OpenMeter customer for per-millisecond compute billing). Per-counter substrate (where beava actually competes): Upstash Redis (de facto edge default), Cloudflare Durable Objects (the structural answer if you're on Cloudflare), Redis-Cell/redis-cell GCRA module, Valkey-on-managed-cache (BSD-3, the cloud-default since 2025), Gubernator (Apache-2.0, sidecar pattern). The bot-defence overlay (Cloudflare BM, DataDome, HUMAN, Kasada, Castle, Fingerprint, Arkose Titan Jan 2026, Wallarm $55 M Series C Jul 2025) sits above the counter store and is not the direct competitor for beava in this segment, but consumes the same per-entity velocity features beava produces - see V3 for that competitive map.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Mixed and the segment is hardening around either 'Apache-2.0 OSS sidecar' or 'proprietary edge-platform-native' poles. The hyperscaler-edge incumbents (Cloudflare Workers Rate Limiting + Durable Objects, Fastly Edge Rate Limiting + KV Store, Akamai EdgeWorkers + EdgeKV + Aggregated Rate Limiting, AWS WAF rate-based rules + API Gateway Usage Plans, Azure Front Door, Netlify Rate Limiting, Vercel Edge Middleware) are uniformly proprietary commercial. The Cloudflare DO SQLite billing flip on Jan 7 2026 makes the structural-on-Cloudflare answer billed, not free, which slightly enlarges the OSS-alternative space. The counter substrate is the locked filter: Upstash Redis is Source Available under Upstash terms and inherits the post-Apr-2024 Redis RSALv2/SSPLv1 (and now Redis 8 tri-license AGPLv3/RSALv2/SSPLv1 since May 2025) controversy through its Redis-protocol parentage; redis-cell GCRA module is BSD-3 but ages-out as Redis itself relicenses; Valkey BSD-3-Clause (Linux Foundation, AWS/Google/Oracle/Percona/Ericsson, default 'redis-server' package in Ubuntu 26.04, AWS ElastiCache for Valkey now default, ~8 percent more ops/s + 22 percent lower p99 + 20 percent lower memory vs Redis OSS) is the procurement-clean drop-in - any 'rolled-own at the edge on Redis' team caught by the relicense is now likely on Valkey. DragonflyDB is BSL (source-available, not OSI). The OSS-sidecar set is Apache-2.0 dominant: Gubernator (Apache-2.0), Envoy Rate Limit (Apache-2.0), Apache APISIX (Apache-2.0, including AI Rate Limiting), NVIDIA go-ratelimit (Apache-2.0), Lago (Apache-2.0), OpenMeter (Apache-2.0), Coraza WAF (Apache-2.0). Kong Rate Limiting Advanced is paywalled to Kong Enterprise. Tyk Pro requires commercial license for DRL features at scale. Beava Apache-2.0 + no open-core posture is a real but no-longer-unique wedge in the segment - it pairs naturally with Valkey/Lago/OpenMeter/Coraza/APISIX/Gubernator as the 'fully OSS edge counter + meter + billing stack' story, which is the structurally correct positioning against the Cloudflare-DO / Upstash / Kong-Enterprise pulls. License posture is a hard buyer filter, not a tiebreaker, in this segment for any team that explicitly does NOT want to be on Cloudflare (sovereign-edge, regulated EU, multi-cloud, on-prem, large telco/ISP).
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: High to Very High - this is among the most-bundled segments in the beava use-case map, second only to V3 bot-defence. Cloudflare bundles five layers (Workers Rate Limiting API free with Workers Paid, Durable Objects SQLite 10 GB/object now-billed from Jan 7 2026 but already included in Workers Paid pricing, WAF Rate Limiting Rules included in zone plans, Bot Management ~$5 k/mo Enterprise add-on, Web Bot Auth + HTTP Message Signatures launched Agents Week 2026 with Amazon/Akamai/OpenAI/AWS WAF/Vercel/Shopify co-adoption, per-customer behavioral baselines Nov 2025) into a single Cloudflare subscription any Cloudflare-fronted enterprise already pays for. Fastly similarly bundles Edge Rate Limiting + KV Store + Compute. AWS bundles WAF rate-based rules + API Gateway Usage Plans (10 k RPS default) + Bot Control. Akamai bundles EdgeWorkers + EdgeKV + Aggregated Rate Limiting (Nov 2025) + Bot Manager + Noname. The bundling threat is structurally HIGHER than at V3 (account-abuse / bot-defence) because the rate-limit primitive sits even deeper in the CDN-already-paid-for-it bundle than the bot-defence ML scorer. The buyers beava CAN still win in this segment, and the reason this segment is winnable at all, are explicitly: (a) non-Cloudflare-fronted infrastructure - Supabase Edge, Vercel Edge (which is on AWS not Cloudflare), Deno Deploy, self-hosted Caddy/Traefik/Nginx/Envoy, Fastly-Compute customers who want to avoid Upstash-Redis license posture, regional ISPs / telcos with on-prem edge, EU-sovereign-edge buyers (DORA / GDPR-tight), (b) usage-meter buyers who need both rate-limit AND exact billing meter in one stack and don't want Kafka+ClickHouse (the Lago/OpenMeter pattern is exactly the alternative beava can fold into one binary), (c) AI-gateway and API-gateway vendors (Kong, Tyk, Apigee, Zuplo, Portkey, Helicone, LiteLLM, TrueFoundry) that want to EMBED a counter+meter backend without depending on a competitor's managed cloud or a Source-Available Redis dependency, (d) the 'rolled-own on Redis+Lua' in-house platform team that just got caught by the Redis-Valkey split. The bundling threat compresses beava's beachhead to non-Cloudflare-fronted and OSS-sovereign-edge buyers - a real but narrower wedge than the bot-defence segment.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Producers in this segment are edge proxies, edge workers, and API gateways emitting per-request events - NOT Kafka/Spark pipelines - which is a strong structural fit for beava's push-on-event model. Expected upstreams: Cloudflare Workers (HTTP fetch outbound only - so beava-from-Worker is HTTP/JSON :8080, NOT framed-TCP), Fastly Compute (HTTP fetch + WASI - same constraint), Vercel Edge Middleware (Edge Runtime, HTTP only), Deno Deploy (HTTP only on edge), Supabase Edge Functions (Deno, HTTP only, 2 s CPU cap), Akamai EdgeWorkers (HTTP only), Netlify Edge Functions (HTTP only), Envoy (access-log filter / ext_proc / Lua filter / WASM filter - can do framed TCP), Nginx (njs / Lua - can do framed TCP), Caddy / HAProxy / Traefik, Kong (Lua / Go plugins - can do framed TCP), Tyk (Go / JS middleware - can do framed TCP), Apigee (JS / Java callouts), AWS API Gateway (Lambda authoriser / WAF rate-based rules), Coraza WAF (proxy-WASM), OPA/Envoy plugin. The CRITICAL ASYMMETRY for this segment: the hyperscaler edge runtimes (Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute, Vercel Edge, Deno Deploy, Supabase Edge, Akamai EdgeWorkers, Netlify Edge) restrict outbound to HTTP / fetch ONLY - beava's framed-TCP+msgpack :8081 (the source of its sub-ms latency edge) CANNOT be reached directly from inside these runtimes, so beava-from-Worker is forced onto HTTP/JSON :8080 which adds milliseconds and erodes the latency advantage. The framed-TCP advantage applies only to (1) self-hosted gateway sidecars (Envoy / Nginx / Kong / Tyk / APISIX), (2) self-hosted edge runtimes (Deno self-host, Supabase self-host, Fastly Compute non-runtime contexts), (3) regional ISP / telco / on-prem edge clusters. Consumers: the same gateway / worker reading get(api_key) on the next request; the usage-billing pipeline (OpenMeter Kafka or HTTP ingest, Lago HTTP ingest, Stripe Meters reporting API, Orb HTTP API) reading aggregated counters at minute / hour cadence; observability (Prometheus / Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry collectors) pulling metrics. CloudEvents is the emerging standard for billing-meter ingest and beava has no documented adapter. The Kafka-first feature-store assumption (Feast / Tecton / Hopsworks) is REVERSED here - rate-limit and meter buyers explicitly do NOT want a broker hop on the inline-decision path, which is exactly the friction beava removes. The friction on the CLIENT side is severe: gateway buyers (Cloudflare, Kong, Tyk, Envoy, APISIX, Zuplo, Caddy) and edge runtimes (Workers, Compute, Vercel Edge, Deno, Supabase, EdgeWorkers) live in Rust / Go / C++ / TypeScript / Lua / WASM, not Python - beava's Python SDK is the wrong-language for any of these buyers; the wire is language-agnostic (TCP+msgpack, HTTP+JSON) but there are no Rust / Go / TypeScript / Lua / WASM SDKs yet.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Mostly rules, with billing-meter pure aggregation and abuse-overlay ML. The rate-limit / quota enforcement path is a deterministic threshold rule (count >= cap => 429, token_bucket_remaining <= 0 => 429, sum_bytes > monthly_quota => suspend) read directly from beava - no scorer involved. The billing-meter path is pure aggregation (sum / count over a tumbling billing-period window) fed into Stripe / OpenMeter / Lago / Orb invoicing - again no scorer. ML scoring shows up only on the abuse-detection overlay (Cloudflare Bot Management ML scorer, DataDome / HUMAN / Kasada / Arkose Titan / Castle / Fingerprint scorers, Cloudflare per-customer behavioral baselines Nov 2025) consuming beava's per-IP velocity / distribution / n_unique HLL features. Beava sits below all three patterns as the substrate and stays decoupled from any scoring engine - the seam is natural and identical across named incumbents.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Seven concrete reasons a non-Cloudflare-fronted or OSS-sovereign buyer in this segment would pick beava over Upstash-Redis-on-Vercel or Cloudflare-DO or Kong-Rate-Limiting-Advanced today: (1) Single binary, no Kafka / Flink / Redis cluster / ClickHouse ceremony - the entire incumbent landscape is two-tier (gateway + external Redis/ClickHouse + sometimes Kafka); beava collapses both the rate-limit counter AND the billing meter into ONE Rust binary. This is uniquely strong vs OpenMeter (Kafka + ClickHouse) and Lago (ClickHouse) and Upstash + a separate meter. (2) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives (count, velocity, sum, distribution, n_unique, recency, distance, entropy, last-N) cover BOTH the rate-limit side (token-bucket / sliding-window / GCRA) AND the usage-meter side (sum_bytes per billing period, sum_tokens per virtual_key per day) in one engine - today buyers stitch redis-cell GCRA + Lua sliding-window for the limit AND Kafka + ClickHouse (OpenMeter) for the meter; beava does both. (3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack matches inline edge latency budget without HTTP overhead - Upstash's HTTP-Redis is connectionless but adds milliseconds; beava's framed-TCP shaves that out, BUT only on self-hosted gateway sidecars and non-Cloudflare-Worker edge runtimes (the hyperscaler-edge runtimes are HTTP-fetch-only outbound, where the wedge collapses to parity with Upstash). (4) Apache-2.0 with NO open-core - strictly more permissive than Upstash-Redis Source-Available, Redis 8 (AGPLv3 / RSALv2 / SSPLv1), Kong Enterprise (paywalled Rate Limiting Advanced), Tyk Pro, DragonflyDB BSL. Comparable only to Valkey, Lago, OpenMeter, Apache APISIX, Gubernator, Envoy Rate Limit, Coraza. Real procurement wedge vs everything-except-Apache-OSS-peers, AND a credible 'embed-without-becoming-Cloudflare-dependent' story for API-gateway vendors (Kong / Tyk / APISIX / Zuplo / Caddy) and AI-gateway vendors (Portkey / Helicone / LiteLLM / TrueFoundry). (5) Push-on-event model maps directly to how edge workers already produce per-request events (Envoy access-log filter, Nginx access_log, Coraza audit log, Cloudflare Worker fetch event) - no broker hop, no broker capex, no Kafka cluster. The model fits Cloudflare DO's per-key actor pattern but without the Cloudflare-vendor-lock. (6) Built-in window semantics (sliding / tumbling / hopping) with the ~\d+(ms|s|m|h|d) DSL rather than rolling-your-own Lua + ZSET trick - this is the same shape Cloudflare DO requires you to hand-code in TypeScript. (7) Refuse-on-network-FS / WAL-on-local-NVMe + single-binary single-region-PoP discipline is exactly the posture Cloudflare's blog 'Counting Things - a lot of different things' describes for its OWN internal per-PoP Rust+Twemproxy+Memcached system - beava ships that architecture as Apache-2.0 OSS, which is uniquely valuable for sovereign-edge / regional-ISP / on-prem / non-Cloudflare buyers who want Cloudflare-grade edge counter architecture without being on Cloudflare. The wedge is concretely strongest for: (i) Supabase / Vercel / Deno self-hosted edge tiers, (ii) regional ISP / telco / EU-sovereign-edge buyers under DORA / GDPR, (iii) the 'I don't want to be on Cloudflare' segment specifically including AI/API gateway vendors that want to embed a counter+meter backend, (iv) the 'rolled-own on Redis+Lua' platform-eng team that just got caught by the Apr-2024 Redis relicense and is looking for an Apache-2.0 alternative that does BOTH rate-limit and billing meter.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete gaps blocking adoption in this segment today, in rough order of pain (derived from use cases 15b and 15c plus 2025-2026 incumbent feature deltas): (1) No TLS / no auth on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 in v0 - DISQUALIFYING for any production edge / CDN / multi-tenant gateway deployment because the rate-limit sidecar inevitably exposes ports to co-tenants and the /admin sidecar on :8090 in particular MUST be locked down before any external buyer will evaluate seriously. Single biggest blocker; even regional-ISP / on-prem buyers expect mTLS between gateway and counter store. (2) No first-class idempotency / dedup-by-event-id primitive - billing meters that feed invoices REQUIRE this (OpenMeter, Lago, Stripe Meters all use event-id-based dedup; OpenMeter retains 32-day dedup window, Stripe 24-hour idempotency keys); without it beava cannot honestly sell the usage-metering side of this segment to SOX/ASC-606 buyers. (3) No multi-tenant namespaces - per-tenant memory and write quotas plus per-tenant rate-limit on the beava admin surface itself, REQUIRED for any PaaS / SaaS / API-gateway vendor running beava for many customer domains to isolate them safely. (4) No async cross-region / cross-PoP counter sync (CRDT-style G-Counter, gossip, log-shipping) - Cloudflare's blog and Tyk DRL design both acknowledge eventual consistency, but at least they ship the convergence; beava v0 does not. Disqualifying for any global single-cap rule ('no customer can exceed 10 M requests/day globally'); Zuplo's pitch is 'globally synchronised across 300+ POPs by default'. (5) No triggers / 'fire when counter crosses threshold' - rate-limit enforcement, budget-alert kill-switches ('when monthly_token_spend > $X, suspend virtual_key'), and Fastly-style penalty-box patterns all want this; today the gateway has to poll. Among the most-cited gaps for the domain. (6) No native integration with the major hyperscaler edge runtimes - Cloudflare Workers and Vercel Edge cannot speak framed TCP (network is HTTP-only outbound outside Durable Objects); HTTP/JSON works but is slower and erodes the latency wedge to parity with Upstash. Requires either a thin HTTP-shim that batches multiple counter ops per request OR explicit 'beava is for self-hosted / non-Cloudflare-edge only' positioning. (7) No Rust / Go / TypeScript / Lua / WASM client SDKs - the buyer ecosystem here lives in proxies and edge runtimes, not Python services; the wire is language-agnostic but the SDK matrix is the gap. Beava's Python SDK is the wrong language for every named edge runtime, API gateway, and AI gateway vendor. (8) No eviction primitives on IP-keyed dimensions (Fastly's 200 k-entries-per-site LRU cap is the explicit model) - cardinality explosion under DDoS-class events can OOM the box; IP cardinality is 10^7-10^10 over a day at edge scale. (9) Per-key TTL with explicit window semantics tied to billing-timezone midnight resets and to billing-period (month-aligned tumbling) boundaries is not first-class. (10) No documented HLL / Bloom / CMS / Top-K primitive prominently in the docs (may exist in the ~60-primitive count but is not surfaced) - (ip x route) cross-product is naively unbounded and these approximate sketches are the fix. (11) In-memory only with WAL + snapshot - billing-grade durability needs a documented cold-start replay-time SLA for tens-of-GB hot meter state, which beava has not published; an edge buyer at hundreds of millions of distinct IPs/day would need sharding and aggressive TTL/eviction to stay in RAM. (12) No reference adapter for OpenMeter / Lago / Stripe Meters CloudEvents event-format. (13) No native PromQL / OpenTelemetry export for the operator-facing rate-limit metrics that gateway buyers expect out of the box (Datadog / Grafana). (14) No streaming admin / debug surface ('top-k api_keys by failure_ratio in last 5 min', 'list all customers within 90 percent of their monthly quota') so operators can drive incident response. (15) Lack of GDPR-friendly defaults (salted-IP-hash-at-rest, short default TTLs, documented PII model) - api_key, IP and customer_id are personal data under GDPR / CCPA. (16) No public edge / gateway case study - Upstash + Cloudflare and Cloudflare Durable Objects both have public production users, beava has none.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Beava-side: NO public beava users on this use case yet; NO dedicated edge / rate-limit / usage-meter demo identified in python/beava/demos/ (the existing demos are python/beava/demos/{adtech, ecommerce, fraud}; the closest analog is the adtech frequency-capping demo which exercises the same primitive shape of counter + window per composite key); NO beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion / case study threads located on this topic. [uncertain] Beava knows WHO the buyer is (platform-engineering / edge-runtime / API-gateway / AI-gateway / usage-billing teams - this is correctly identified in use case 15c) and the ~60-primitive operator catalogue is a near-exact shape match for the published primitive shapes of Fastly ratecounter (1 s / 10 s / 60 s overlapping buckets per key with LRU eviction at 200 k entries) and Upstash-ratelimit-js (sliding-window / token-bucket / fixed-window per identifier). A dedicated examples/edge-rate-limit/ or examples/usage-metering/ with a mock Cloudflare Worker / Express / FastAPI gateway pushing per-request events and reading back token-bucket state would be a 1-2 day authoring task that the use-case research explicitly recommends. External validation that the SHAPE is right (not that beava itself has traction): Cloudflare's published blog 'Counting Things - a lot of different things' describes the largest CDN in the world building exactly the architecture beava ships (per-PoP Rust + in-memory counter + async cross-PoP convergence); Fastly Edge Rate Limiting GA + ratecounter validates the 200 k-entries-per-site LRU constraint shape; Cloudflare Workers Rate Limiting GA Sept 19 2025 + Durable Objects SQLite 10 GB cap + billing flip Jan 7 2026 + Durable Object Facets at Agents Week 2026 validate the per-tenant isolated counter design point; Akamai Aggregated Rate Limiting (Nov 2025), Zuplo globally-synchronised rate limiting across 300+ POPs, AWS WAF rate-based rules, Cloudflare Bot Management per-customer behavioral baselines (Nov 2025), and Web Bot Auth / HTTP Message Signatures (Agents Week 2026, co-adopted by Amazon / Akamai / OpenAI / AWS WAF / Vercel / Shopify) collectively validate 'edge-native per-customer rate-limit' as a 2025-2026 competitive-feature checkbox every edge platform now has to ship; Stripe acquiring Metronome (Jan 2026) and Stripe Billing Meter Events v2 + OpenMeter's 'millions of usage events per minute' + Lago 1 M EPS + Trigger.dev as a named OpenMeter customer for per-millisecond compute billing collectively validate the usage-meter side as a fast-growing 2025-2026 market; Apache APISIX AI Rate Limiting (token-level, Apache-2.0, 100+ plugins zero paywall) and Helicone token-based per-user rate limiting and Cloudflare AI Gateway rate limiting all validate the per-token, per-virtual-key AI-gateway sub-segment as a brand-new ~2024-2026 category. Upstash @upstash/ratelimit is the de facto serverless rate-limit library across Vercel / Cloudflare / Deno / Netlify / Supabase ecosystems - the named open-source competitor against which beava's primitive catalogue + single-binary + Apache-2.0 wedge would be benchmarked. The market validation is overwhelming; the beava-specific traction in this segment is zero.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Compete (focused). Lead-eligible on technical fit (the ~60-primitive operator catalogue is a near-exact shape match for what Fastly ratecounter and Upstash-ratelimit and OpenMeter productise, AND beava is uniquely positioned to fold the rate-limit and usage-meter into ONE binary which no incumbent does), market urgency (2025-2026 has Cloudflare Workers Rate Limiting GA, Cloudflare DO SQLite billing flip Jan 2026, Akamai Aggregated Rate Limiting Nov 2025, Web Bot Auth at Agents Week 2026, Stripe acquiring Metronome Jan 2026, the LLM token-counter retrofit across every AI gateway, and the Redis-Valkey license split all converging), and Apache-2.0 wedge against Upstash-Redis / Kong-Enterprise / Tyk-Pro / DragonflyDB-BSL / Cloudflare-DO-vendor-lock. Downgraded from Lead to Compute because (a) hyperscaler bundling threat is HIGH-to-VERY-HIGH (Cloudflare Workers RL + DO + WAF + BM + Web Bot Auth bundle is the buyer-default for any Cloudflare-fronted enterprise), (b) zero beava-side traction / no dedicated demo / no public case study, (c) the framed-TCP latency wedge collapses inside the hyperscaler-edge runtimes (Workers / Vercel Edge / Deno / Supabase Edge / EdgeWorkers are HTTP-fetch-only outbound) so the realistic motion is FOCUSED on (i) Supabase / Vercel / Deno self-hosted edge, (ii) self-hosted gateway sidecars (Envoy / Nginx / Kong / Tyk / APISIX), (iii) sovereign-edge / regional-ISP / on-prem / EU-DORA buyers, (iv) AI/API gateway vendors that want to embed a counter+meter backend without becoming Cloudflare-dependent or Upstash-Redis-Source-Available-licensed. Pursue actively as a wedge IF beava ships: TLS+auth (item 1), idempotency-by-event-id (item 2), multi-tenant namespaces (item 3), threshold-crossing triggers (item 5), Rust + Go + TypeScript SDKs (item 7), prominently-documented HLL/CMS (item 10), and ONE credible design-partner-shaped demo (single-binary edge counter + billing meter against a Supabase or Vercel-Edge workload). The 'OSS-edge / sovereign-edge / not-on-Cloudflare' wedge is real but narrower than the bot-defence segment (V3) - this is a focused Compete, not a Lead.
